comments.body: thinking of instead adding a bool regex param to these functions

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`split()` and `replace()` now match literally, with `regex=true` to opt into pattern matching. `matches()` is unchanged and stays regex-always.

This card started as "add `escape_regex()`". Its own diagnosis was that each string function's needle semantics is a separate thing to memorize - `count` and `index_of` literal, `replace` regex, `split` regex-if-it-compiles - and `escape_regex()` adds a fourth thing to memorize plus a ritual to remember at every call site. We fixed the default instead.

A survey of every `split`/`replace` call with a string-literal pattern across the ~500 `.rad` scripts on this machine:

|         | literal | regex |
|---------|---------|-------|
| replace | 158     | 25    |
| split   | 10      | 1     |

87% wanted literal. The failure is also asymmetric: literal-when-you-wanted-regex gives an obviously wrong answer, regex-when-you-wanted-literal corrupts silently. `docs-web/docs/examples/hm.md:61` already shipped `base_name.replace(".txt", "")` in our own docs, working only by luck.

Three things fell out that `escape_regex()` could not have delivered:

- `split()`'s runtime-decided semantics is gone. Under `regex=true` an uncompilable pattern errors instead of silently falling back to `strings.Split`.
- `replace()`'s replacement string is literal by default, so `$1` or `$$` in relayed prose stops corrupting the result. That was the original card's headline failure mode.
- The 87% path no longer compiles a regex at all and can no longer throw RAD20024.

---

### What shipped

- `split(_val, _sep, *, limit, regex: bool = false)` and `replace(_original, _find, _replace, *, regex: bool = false)`.
- `replace()`'s group expansion rewritten as a single left-to-right scan, fixing four latent bugs in the old per-group `strings.ReplaceAll` loop: `$10` corrupted by the `$1` pass, a submatch containing `$2` re-substituted by a later pass, no way to write a literal `$`, and groups read by re-running the pattern against the matched text in isolation, which came back empty whenever an assertion only held in context (`\Bb(c)` inside `abc`). Rules are now `$$`, `${N}`, `$N` taking the longest digit run, and an out-of-range group left as written. Go's own `Regexp.Expand` was not used, because it reads `$name` as a run of word characters and would break the documented `"$1o$1"` -> `"bob"` case.
- RAD40016, a checker warning flagging literal patterns that read as regexes with no `regex=`. Warning severity, on by default, handles UFCS call sites, and reads the literal segments of interpolated patterns. Deliberately quiet on a bare `.` and a lone `|`. Lives in its own file, `rts/check/check_regex_migration.go`, so it can be deleted whole in a release or two.
- `docs-web/docs/migrations/v0.12.md`, `core/error_docs/40016.md`, and a new "Patterns: Literal by Default" section in the strings guide.

### Verified

`make all` green. On the real corpus the warning found 32 affected call sites with zero false positives and zero misses. Sharp edges exercised directly: `$10` with ten groups, a submatch whose text contains `$2`, `$$`, `${N}` (which needs a raw string or `$\{1}` to survive Rad's own interpolation), an out-of-range `$99`, and both uncompilable-pattern error paths.

### Follow-ups opened

- `escape_regex()` demoted to p2. Still useful for *building* patterns (`"^" + escape_regex(prefix)`), but no longer the fix for this friction. `fr`'s hand-rolled helper disappears entirely.
- `replace()` declares `-> str` while its `regex=true` path can error, unlike `matches()` (`bool|error`). Left alone here because widening it pushes an error union into every existing call site.
title: Flip split() and replace() to literal-by-default
